visual_cues: Use a column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, asymmetric composition, and generous negative space. Set left-aligned sans-serif type with clear size hierarchy; use black and white with restrained accent colors and grid-aligned photography. Animate along layout axes and settle elements on shared alignment points without disrupting reading order.
note: A supplemental design reference; not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection.

tech.implementation: Build typography with CSS Grid and loaded fonts. Align SVG geometry to the baseline grid; animate position, scale, and cropping.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to International Typographic Style (Swiss Style) without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Use a column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, asymmetric composition, and generous negative space. Set left-aligned sans-serif type with clear size hierarchy; use black and white with restrained accent colors and grid-aligned photography. Animate along layout axes and settle elements on shared alignment points without disrupting reading order. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Build typography with CSS Grid and loaded fonts. Align SVG geometry to the baseline grid; animate position, scale, and cropping. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a horizontal card track that moves with swipe or drag and settles at a defined snap selection. Preserve readable cards, accessible navigation, and one track-position owner; author the track directly for video.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.

audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. avoid: Multi-hue categorical palettes imported from the data style
Decorative chart animation without a stated value

supporting_styles.role: Headline and statement motion

suggestions.html_application: Hero headlines animate into place on load or scroll with real DOM text, remain selectable, and render as the final static layout under reduced motion.
consistency_rules: One sans-serif family with weight and size steps only.

Reading order never changes mid-animation.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

supporting_styles.role: Headline and slogan motion: timing, scale and holds for cutout words

suggestions.rationale: Kinetic timing gives punk cutout lettering readable beats without smoothing away the irregular paste-up placement.
suggestions.best_for: Lyric clips, manifesto reels, gig or campaign announcements.
suggestions.video_application: Paste each cutout word on a beat with a small fixed offset and rotation, hold the full slogan, then tear away to the next layout; motion stays abrupt, never springy.
suggestions.html_application: Hero slogans assemble word by word on scroll or button press; prefers-reduced-motion shows the finished paste-up, and the real text stays in the DOM for screen readers.
consistency_rules: Only #EFE9D9, #171717 and #C63A3A; red marks at most one word per slogan.
Cutout letters use precomputed Pillow torn masks with fixed seeds.
Kinetic moves are limited to paste, tear and peel; no smooth tracking or blur.
avoid: Ransom lettering that buries the key word

supporting_styles.role: Photo treatment: monochrome halftone for cutout photographs

suggestions.rationale: Halftone gives every pasted photo the same photocopied print language, so mixed source images read as one artifact.
suggestions.best_for: Band histories, archival protest stories, editorial collage intros.
suggestions.video_application: Photos arrive as halftoned #171717 cutouts with dots anchored to the image while they slide or tape down; red appears only as a marker scrawl over the halftone.
suggestions.html_application: Gallery cards render halftone via a precomputed image or SVG pattern and stay static on hover; alt text describes the original photo content.
consistency_rules: Halftone dots use #171717 on #EFE9D9 only; no CMYK separations.
One fixed dot angle and size per piece, scaled with the artwork.

Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. 1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Use fine graphite lines, exploratory contours, and localized hatching on pale paper. Build volume through pencil marks rather than broad digital gradients. Reveal lines in drawing order or alternate controlled drawing variations while keeping pressure and texture coherent. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Prepare paper textures and graphite brushes. Layer contours and hatching; use designed drawing variants rather than arbitrary noise. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.

Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.

Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional sketch rendering: when the brief calls for sketch-like marks, consult the Rough.js entry in tech.recommended_stack. Use package roughjs to generate seeded Canvas/SVG geometry, preserve the resolved palette, and follow its style_application and integration_guidance. Cache shapes; let the selected timeline animate transforms, masks, reveals or authored pose variants. Rough.js does not supply handwriting, authentic drawing media, a character rig or frame-by-frame poses. Keep precise text, measured geometry and approved source assets intact.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

visual_cues: Use a clean pale background, simplified line diagrams, and legible lettering. Draw only objects that help explain the subject. Reveal diagrams in causal order, then add annotations; use erasure or redrawing transitions with sufficient reading pauses.
note: The source directly names or describes this visual direction. A whiteboard animation does not require a fabricated drawing hand.

tech.implementation: Organize diagram paths and text layers in advance. Reveal them in explanatory order; do not invent a drawing hand when none is provided.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Whiteboard Animation without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Whiteboard Animation video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. 1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Use a clean pale background, simplified line diagrams, and legible lettering. Draw only objects that help explain the subject. Reveal diagrams in causal order, then add annotations; use erasure or redrawing transitions with sufficient reading pauses. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Organize diagram paths and text layers in advance. Reveal them in explanatory order; do not invent a drawing hand when none is provided. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.

Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional sketch rendering: when the brief calls for sketch-like marks, consult the Rough.js entry in tech.recommended_stack. Use package roughjs to generate seeded Canvas/SVG geometry, preserve the resolved palette, and follow its style_application and integration_guidance. Cache shapes; let the selected timeline animate transforms, masks, reveals or authored pose variants. Rough.js does not supply handwriting, authentic drawing media, a character rig or frame-by-frame poses. Keep precise text, measured geometry and approved source assets intact.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Cytoscape.js option: For scenes containing meaningful node-edge relationships, optionally select Cytoscape.js from tech.recommended_stack. Compute relationship diagram structure and positions, then render authored SVG or Canvas strokes in explanatory drawing order; retain whiteboard typography and stroke treatment. Follow its graph validation, layout, algorithm and rendering guidance. Cache layouts and analysis, drive highlights and movement from composition time, and preserve exact graph meaning, palette tokens, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline. Use a custom visual renderer where required by the style.
Anime.js option: Optionally select Anime.js from tech.recommended_stack when its documented animation features help the scene. Reveal prepared SVG diagram strokes in explanatory order, retaining authored text and reading holds. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Retain the selected framework render_pipeline and the HyperFrames GSAP master timeline contract; use Anime.js only through a verified time adapter with separate property ownership. Preserve palette tokens, exact copy, shared_motion_guidance and style cadence.
Paper.js option: Optionally select Paper.js from tech.recommended_stack when vector path geometry or Canvas rendering is useful. Prepare diagram paths and sample path length for deterministic drawing reveals; retain explanatory order and readable labels. Follow its suggested_methods, integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Evaluate geometry from fixed rest states at composition time, explicitly update the view, and preserve palette tokens, original contour character, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

visual_cues: Use clear flat color fields, simplified figures, consistent corner radii, and three to five main colors with a fixed accent. Keep icons, outlines, and typography proportionally consistent. Communicate through movement, masks, decomposition, and meaningful morphs; stage entrances and hold key text. Avoid photorealistic reflections, complex materials, and inconsistent shadows.
note: A supplemental design reference; not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection. Using SVG does not establish this aesthetic. User-requested guidance does not establish that every suggested detail was verified in the source video.

tech.implementation: Use SVG primitives and groups for flat artwork. Animate easing, masks, paths, and semantically clear shape transformations.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Flat Vector Illustration without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Flat Vector Illustration video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Use clear flat color fields, simplified figures, consistent corner radii, and three to five main colors with a fixed accent. Keep icons, outlines, and typography proportionally consistent. Communicate through movement, masks, decomposition, and meaningful morphs; stage entrances and hold key text. Avoid photorealistic reflections, complex materials, and inconsistent shadows. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Use SVG primitives and groups for flat artwork. Animate easing, masks, paths, and semantically clear shape transformations. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional mo.js effects: consult the @mojs/core entry in tech.recommended_stack when shape, burst, swirl or HTML effects support the scene. Follow its style_application, integration_guidance, determinism_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve the resolved palette and reading holds. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and drive progress from shared composition time; verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks. Keep one owner per animated property and preserve the selected video framework lifecycle. Do not use live click triggers or regeneration during video export. Use the existing GSAP/SVG route if an effect cannot satisfy deterministic seeking.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Cytoscape.js option: For scenes containing meaningful node-edge relationships, optionally select Cytoscape.js from tech.recommended_stack. Lay out node-link illustrations with flat shapes, clear arrows and approved colors; use graph logic only for scenes that actually contain relationships. Follow its graph validation, layout, algorithm and rendering guidance. Cache layouts and analysis, drive highlights and movement from composition time, and preserve exact graph meaning, palette tokens, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline. Use a custom visual renderer where required by the style.
Anime.js option: Optionally select Anime.js from tech.recommended_stack when its documented animation features help the scene. Animate flat SVG shapes, grouped transforms and masks while preserving approved colors. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Retain the selected framework render_pipeline and the HyperFrames GSAP master timeline contract; use Anime.js only through a verified time adapter with separate property ownership. Preserve palette tokens, exact copy, shared_motion_guidance and style cadence.
Paper.js option: Optionally select Paper.js from tech.recommended_stack when vector path geometry or Canvas rendering is useful. Build flat vector shapes, groups and clipping masks, using boolean operations where the artwork needs them. Follow its suggested_methods, integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Evaluate geometry from fixed rest states at composition time, explicitly update the view, and preserve palette tokens, original contour character, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Anime video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. 1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Choose a coherent anime character-design and rendering language, including stable proportions, expressive poses, clean linework, and controlled shadow shapes. Plan key poses, holds, and selectively detailed action. Avoid treating all anime as one aesthetic or claiming that a static cel-shading filter constitutes character animation. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Prepare consistent character drawings or frame sequences, optionally in Krita. Composite designed poses and timing rather than relying on a single filtered image. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Choose oil painting or gouache as the primary medium. Keep lighting and palette coherent, and animate repainting, brush reveals, or layered scenery without forcing both material behaviors onto every object. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.

Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.

visual_cues: Choose charcoal or pastel as the primary medium. Charcoal emphasizes tonal mass, hatching, and smudging; pastel allows softly layered pigment with visible grain. Preserve paper texture and localized powder edges while revealing or erasing marks; avoid uniform noise that obscures structure.
note: A supplemental design reference; not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection. Charcoal and pastel are separate dry-media techniques.

tech.implementation: Use fixed grain brushes, smudge masks, and paper layers. Build charcoal values or pastel color layers separately and reveal marks locally.

An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Chinese Calligraphy without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Compose around authentic calligraphic gesture, character spacing, and negative space. Vertical text, vermilion seals, and limited imagery may support the piece. Select a consistent script and accurate wording; reveal complete groups or follow actual stroke order without stretching characters into incorrect forms. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Use authentic calligraphy assets or verified glyph paths. Writing animation requires separate stroke paths in the correct order; outlining a font is not equivalent to animating brush strokes. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

tech.implementation: Generate thick paperboard geometry, creases, and seams in Blender. Use paper materials and soft light; animate hinges and assembly joints.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. 2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Show paper fibers, cardboard thickness, folds, cuts, and assembly seams. Use soft lighting and colors that suit the material. Assemble or unfold parts along plausible connections; maintain consistent thickness rather than deforming cardboard like rubber. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Generate thick paperboard geometry, creases, and seams in Blender. Use paper materials and soft light; animate hinges and assembly joints. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
