tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.

An explicitly authored demonstration cue table (JSON: contact time, contact point, note, duration, labeled 'demo, not analyzed') becomes GSAP labels. Account for sample attack. Never use live Web Audio analysis during export. Reviewed technology choice: Silent 3s preview of the collision instrument: background #F3EBDD with an SVG ball (#293B44) dropping onto three tuned bars (#628C98, #BA7B61). An explicitly authored demonstration cue table (JSON: contact time, contact point, note, duration, labeled 'demo, not analyzed') becomes GSAP labels. Each contact visibly causes a response: bar compression, then a ripple ring, then the bar brightens for the note duration. Impacts read before the rebound, density varies, and there is a pause before the final hit. Full video: Python librosa beat_track/onset_detect and NumPy band RMS run offline, beats are manually verified, and the shared JSON drives both the GSAP visuals and HyperFrames audio placement. Account for sample attack. Never use live Web Audio analysis during export. The mechanical-sculpture recipe uses the same cue table, with bass, transient and treble mapped to separate bounded part owners, and parts return to rest in breaks. The style is a timing discipline layered over another visual style, so the renderer is light and the shared offline cue table is central. SVG is enough for a clear contact-to-response chain. A 3D renderer would only be chosen if the underlying brief demands depth. Web Audio is limited to authoring inspection. mo.js bursts were rejected to avoid a second clock. FFmpeg is redundant with HyperFrames audio.
Optional recipe collision_instrument: Each visible contact causes a corresponding note. Save collision time, contact point, note onset and duration in one offline cue table. Account for audio sample attack and ensure impacts read before rebound. Silent previews must visibly show the contact-to-response chain; full videos use the verified cues for audio.
Optional recipe audio_reactive_sculpture: Map measured low/mid/high frequency bands and amplitude envelopes to named mechanical parts. Bass extension, transient opening and upper-band brightness have distinct owners and bounded ranges. Save analysis offline and evaluate it from shared composition time; do not use live audio analysis during export. Breakdowns/silence return parts to rest without fighting the main timeline. Silent previews can use an explicitly authored demonstration cue table, not imply a real analyzed track.

tech.implementation:
Background #F4EDDF and floor line #32444A. Two contrasting bodies, a #66978E ball and a #C78461 jelly block, each in nested <g> elements: an outer group for translation and an inner group for squash with transform-origin at the contact point. Key poses: anticipation (sy 0.85) → fall with stretch along velocity (sy 1.25) → impact (sx 1.3, sy 1/1.3, so area is preserved) → rebound → short hold → settle. Timing differs per object, and only one object deforms at a time. GSAP keyframes on the paused timeline; volume is checked by asserting sx·sy≈1 at sampled seeks. 3s preview: ball cycle 0–1.6s, block hop 1.4–2.6s, hold. Optional MorphSVGPlugin for contact-flattened silhouettes between compatible paths. Soft-body/glass recipe for full video: Three.js with MeshPhysicalMaterial on a deformed mesh, with XPBD fixed-step states baked and seeked from cache, labeled an approximation.
Optional recipe soft_body_glass: Use contact-aware deformation and apparent volume conservation with damped settling, not global scale pulsing. Combine Liquid Glass 069 when clear transmission is requested. XPBD is already in the technology pool: initialize once, cache/bake fixed-step states and support direct/backward seeking. Keep optical contours aligned with the deformed surface. Label analytic shape-key previews as soft-body approximations, not measured physical simulation.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: This is a motion principle, so a clean, inspectable 2D renderer with explicit pivots shows it most faithfully in 3 seconds. Uniform spring presets are rejected. suggestions.video_application: Animate word groups (not single glyphs) with scale-Y compression at the baseline pivot, one key word at a time, and hold each settled word for at least a beat before the next one enters.
suggestions.html_application: Hero heading entrance driven by scroll or load on a seekable timeline, with real DOM text for screen readers and a static fallback when motion is reduced.
consistency_rules: Text in #32444A on #F4EDDF; accents mark emphasis words only.
Deform from baseline pivots and return to exact glyph proportions at rest.
One emphasis word bounces per phrase.
avoid: Stretching body copy or small text past legibility.
Continuous wobble after the word has settled.

visual_cues: Establish shared color, line, texture, and lighting rules before mixing photos, drawings, paper, type, or 3D objects. Give each medium a narrative role and connect them through composition, direction, and intentional transitions. Retain medium differences within a coherent whole.
note: The label has been normalized from source descriptions or references. A mixed-media request does not establish that physical stop-motion footage was used.

tech.implementation: Preprocess photography, drawings, and paper assets for consistent color, edges, and dimensions. Prerender 3D elements as transparent sequences when needed and composite them with text and images.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Mixed-Media Animation without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Mixed-Media Animation video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Establish shared color, line, texture, and lighting rules before mixing photos, drawings, paper, type, or 3D objects. Give each medium a narrative role and connect them through composition, direction, and intentional transitions. Retain medium differences within a coherent whole. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Preprocess photography, drawings, and paper assets for consistent color, edges, and dimensions. Prerender 3D elements as transparent sequences when needed and composite them with text and images. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional sketch rendering: when the brief calls for sketch-like marks, consult the Rough.js entry in tech.recommended_stack. Use package roughjs to generate seeded Canvas/SVG geometry, preserve the resolved palette, and follow its style_application and integration_guidance. Cache shapes; let the selected timeline animate transforms, masks, reveals or authored pose variants. Rough.js does not supply handwriting, authentic drawing media, a character rig or frame-by-frame poses. Keep precise text, measured geometry and approved source assets intact.
Optional PhotoSwipe gallery: use the PhotoSwipe entry in tech only when interactive web delivery requires an image lightbox. Follow its style_application, import_guidance, integration_guidance and selection_guidance. Supply accurate image dimensions, responsive sources, fallback links and usable navigation; preserve image colors and the resolved palette. For video, follow video_guidance and author swipe, zoom and thumbnail transitions on the shared composition timeline instead of running a live lightbox.
Optional crop preparation: consult Cropper.js in tech.recommended_stack when raster assets need interactive crop authoring. Follow its style_application, api_version_guidance, integration_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve original assets, approved colors, essential subject context and motion overscan; record the source, selection, transforms, coordinate system and output size. Await export and inspect actual framing and image quality. For video, follow video_guidance and use a saved asset or reproducible crop recipe on the shared composition timeline. Cropper.js does not supply subject extraction, background removal or missing parallax artwork.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Dragula option: For interactive delivery or an accompanying editor, optionally select Dragula from tech.recommended_stack. Optional reordering of asset cards in an accompanying browser editor; not freeform collage positioning. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification. For rendered video, use authored timeline gestures and deterministic layout states; do not depend on live dragging. Preserve palette tokens, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Mixed-Media Animation, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.

Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

supporting_styles.role: Annotation layer: handwritten labels, circles and arrows that link photo, paper and drawn elements to the narrative.

suggestions.rationale: A single handwritten voice stitches different media together and explains why each one is on screen, without adding another material.
suggestions.best_for: Documentary-style brand stories and research summaries built from supplied photos and sketches.

One handwriting stroke width and one hand-style for the whole piece.
Annotations appear after the medium they describe, never before.
avoid: Using handwriting as a fourth decorative texture with no reference.
Retinting supplied photos outside the primary palette grade.

supporting_styles.role: Camera and spatial treatment: restrained layered parallax that separates photo, paper and drawn planes.

suggestions.rationale: Parallax depth turns flat collage layers into a single, readable space and gives the shared composition a consistent motion direction.
suggestions.best_for: Opening sequences and chapter transitions in heritage, culture or editorial pieces.

consistency_rules: Depth order maps to narrative role, not to the medium's file type.
One light direction and shadow softness across all planes.
Parallax offsets stay small so edges never reveal blank canvas.
avoid: Deep camera moves that need missing background plates.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a horizontal card track that moves with swipe or drag and settles at a defined snap selection. Preserve readable cards, accessible navigation, and one track-position owner; author the track directly for video.

Consider a cohesive orb deformed through bounded vertex displacement or compact metaballs. Keep the form connected and time-evaluated. Energy styling, blue, and glow are optional; this visual treatment does not establish physical fluid behavior.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

visual_cues: Animate deliberate stretching, stringing, merging, splitting, and elastic settling of droplets or viscous forms. Choose a 2D or 3D surface language and keep highlights from obscuring contours. A drop may land, spread, and gather into a wordmark; hold accurate lettering after formation. SDF metaballs simulate a fluid appearance without establishing physically accurate fluid behavior.
note: A user-requested direction developed into practical prompt guidance. A motion vocabulary that can be 2D or 3D; it does not require glass, iridescence, or physically validated fluid simulation.

tech.implementation: Build metaballs from SDF circles or spheres with smooth unions and time-driven position, radius, and stretch. Use full-screen shading for 2D or ray marching with distance-field normals for 3D. Use verified glyph distance fields or composite real text after formation. For physical splashes and collisions, simulate and bake in Blender.
alternatives: Blender Baked Fluid Simulation + Python bpy
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Animate deliberate stretching, stringing, merging, splitting, and elastic settling of droplets or viscous forms. Choose a 2D or 3D surface language and keep highlights from obscuring contours. A drop may land, spread, and gather into a wordmark; hold accurate lettering after formation. Use full-screen shading for 2D or ray marching with distance-field normals for 3D. Use verified glyph distance fields or composite real text after formation. For physical splashes and collisions, simulate and bake in Blender. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.

Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
p5.js option: If useful, select the p5.js entry in tech.recommended_stack for the visual layer. Create stylized blobs, noise-driven contours or custom WebGL shaders; p5.js is not itself a physical fluid solver, viscosity model or surface-merging algorithm. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification, and use the selected framework composition time for redraws. Keep all approved palette colors and existing style cadence unchanged.
Paper.js option: Optionally select Paper.js from tech.recommended_stack when vector path geometry or Canvas rendering is useful. Optionally animate stylized organic vector contours from fixed geometry; boolean merges can change topology and need prepared or cached states, not assumptions of physical fluid behavior. Follow its suggested_methods, integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Evaluate geometry from fixed rest states at composition time, explicitly update the view, and preserve palette tokens, original contour character, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

supporting_styles.role: Typography: real-font kinetic text that takes over once the liquid gathers into a wordmark or phrase.

tech.implementation:
Fixed 1920x1080 composition with a full-bleed #1B3ED2 rect as the opaque scene field (never cream). Everything is drawn in a single SVG with viewBox in drafting units (1 unit = 1 mm at a fixed scale).

Layers:
- Minor and major white grid lines (stroke-opacity 0.25 / 0.5).
- Object outlines at 2.5px.
- Hidden edges as stroke-dasharray '8 6' at 1.5px.
- Section hatching as a 45° <pattern> of 1px lines, clipped to closed regions.
- Dimension lines with extension lines.

All geometry comes from one measured spec object, so label text is computed from the real dimensions. Labels are HTML/CSS (or SVG text) in a monospaced/technical face, with each label annotated data-reveal-after="dim-N".

Motion: one paused GSAP timeline registered as window.__timelines[id].
1. Grid fades in.
2. Outlines draw with DrawSVGPlugin ('0% 0%' → '0% 100%').
3. Hidden edges draw. Dashing is a mask over a fully drawn dashed path, so it never conflicts with the drawSVG dasharray.
4. The hatch clip rect wipes in.
5. Dimension shafts draw from both ends toward their arrows.

Arrowheads are separate <path data-arrowhead-for="dim-N"> elements, set to autoAlpha 0 and switched on with gsap.set at the exact time the shaft's drawSVG reaches 100%. Each label appears only after its dimension line and both heads are complete.

Preview (3 s): one part view, about 4 dimensions, hatching and labels.
Full video: chains views through labels on the same timeline.

Verify forward, backward and direct seeks at the head-switch times. Use chroma_js to confirm the white-on-blue contrast of 7.88.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection:
Measured geometry with readable labels is crisp vector plus real-text territory. SVG keeps dimensions exact and HTML/CSS keeps text measurable. DrawSVGPlugin gives seekable stroke reveals on the HyperFrames GSAP clock.

Alternatives considered:
- Canvas 2D would lose text accessibility and crisp scaling.
- Manim would replace the pipeline.
- Rough.js would destroy precision.
- d3 scales are unnecessary for fixed drafting units.

Tradeoff: dense hatching patterns can alias, so pattern spacing should be checked at 1080p.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Blueprint Drafting Animation without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.

motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

visual_cues: Black field with cyan contours, narrow white cores and horizontal scan-line fills. Light is communicated through line density, without blur halos or generic neon particles.
note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
A Canvas 2D renderer at a devicePixelRatio-fixed backing size. Each frame clears to opaque #07080A. Subjects are authored as Path2D outlines (head/object contours) cached once.

Render per frame from progress values:
1. Scanline fill: clip to the Path2D, then fillRect horizontal 1px lines of #45F0DD every N px, pixel-aligned to integer rows. Line spacing varies with an authored 'light' value per region, so denser lines read as brighter and sparser as darker. Light is communicated only by line density.
2. Contour: stroke the path twice, cyan #45F0DD at 3px, then a white #FFFFFF core at 1px.
3. Optional faint cyan grid behind.

No shadowBlur, no bloom, no particles.

GSAP owns a plain state object, tweened on the paused registered timeline: contour reveal (setLineDash-based length progress from path lengths precomputed via an offscreen SVG getTotalLength), scanline wipe y-extent, and density shifts. A single render(state) is called from the timeline's onUpdate and also after any seek, so direct seeks are exact. Any interior labels use data-reveal-after on their container frame.

Preview (3 s): one subject outline draws, scanlines sweep in top-to-bottom, then density modulates.
Full video: reuses the renderer with more paths.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection:
Pixel-aligned scanlines clipped to shapes are cheapest and crispest in Canvas 2D, with exact control over line density.

Alternatives considered:
- SVG pattern fills would work but scale or anti-alias scanlines unevenly under transforms.
- WebGL/GLSL is overkill for flat line art.
- UnrealBloom and Points are excluded because the style forbids blur halos and neon particles.

Tradeoff: Canvas text is less accessible, so keep captions as DOM overlays if needed.

motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

visual_cues: Sharp silhouettes with a black-to-red-to-orange-to-cream heat ramp, cool narrow extremities and authored hotspots. Distinguish thermal illustration from measured temperature data.
note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Three.js WebGLRenderer with an orthographic fullscreen quad and a ShaderMaterial, cleared to opaque #080808.

Canvas 2D rasterizes the authored sharp silhouette (head profile) once into a mask CanvasTexture, plus a blurred distance-like copy for interior falloff. The fragment shader computes heat as:
- the interior falloff (core warmer than edges),
- plus authored Gaussian hotspots (uniform arrays: position, radius, intensity),
- minus cooling at narrow extremities (nose, ears) from a thinness term,
- plus slow seeded value-noise shimmer evaluated from uTime.

Heat is mapped through a 4-stop ramp texture (1D DataTexture) precomputed with chroma.scale(['#080808','#C82E20','#F07C30','#FFF1D5']).mode('lab'). The ramp applies only inside the silhouette mask, and edges stay sharp via the hard mask alpha.

GSAP tweens a uniform-state object (hotspot intensities, warm-up progress, uTime) on the paused registered timeline. onUpdate writes the uniforms and calls renderer.render, so seeks are exact.

No temperature scale, degrees or legend is shown: this is illustrative heat, not measured data.

Preview (3 s): the silhouette warms from black through red to cream hotspots.
Full video: alternating paper/red scenes are separate clips; the thermal clip keeps black.

tech.implementation:
Opaque porcelain #F0EEE6 field, with graphite #222522 engraved linework in SVG:
- Number wheels: circles with radial tick paths, and digits placed around the rim as SVG text in a tabular face.
- Inspection rails: parallel lines with notch marks.
- Belts: a closed path around two pulleys with tooth marks along a dashed stroke.
- Engraving shading: fine parallel-line <pattern> fills clipped to bevel regions.

Accents: green #416B53 marks the inspection pointer and orange #E78636 marks the active digit. Readouts are HTML/CSS with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

Motion: a single GSAP driver value `drive` (degrees of the input crank) on the paused registered timeline. In onUpdate, every linked part is derived kinematically from it:
- wheel B rotation = -drive * (rA/rB),
- belt tooth stroke-dashoffset = drive * rA * π/180,
- the rail carriage translates by belt travel,
- the wheel digit settles with a detent ease when it crosses a step.

Because no part has its own independent tween, the movement explains a real operation (e.g. a carry: one full units revolution advances the tens wheel one step). Engraved contours first draw in with DrawSVGPlugin.

Any pointer arrows use a separate data-arrowhead-for head, shown only when the shaft completes. Wheel labels use data-reveal-after on their wheel group.

Preview (3 s): a units wheel turns through 9→0 and carries the tens wheel one detent while the belt advances the rail.
Full video: adds operations using the same driver pattern.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection:
Engraved line art and tabular numerals need crisp vectors and real text. Deriving all linked motion from one GSAP-owned driver guarantees coherent, explanatory mechanics and exact seeking.

Alternatives considered:
- Three.js 3D gears would shift the look away from flat engraving.
- Manim would replace the pipeline.
- MorphSVG is inappropriate because mechanical parts move rigidly.
- Tonal hatching shaders are designed for 3D luminance, not engraved regions.

Tradeoff: fine engraving patterns need moiré checks at output size.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Engraved Mechanical Diagrams without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

tech.implementation:
Three.js fullscreen-quad ShaderMaterial that raymarches an SDF scene: a Mandelbox/Mandelbulb-style fractal solid with a bounded iteration count (e.g. 8 fractal iterations, max 96 march steps, max distance clamp).

Shading:
- normals by central differences,
- one reflection bounce by re-marching along reflect(rd, n) with a reduced step budget,
- soft AO approximated by a few SDF samples,
- exponential distance fog toward #080A0C.

The scene is rendered into a WebGLRenderTarget at about 0.5–0.66 scale and upsampled to the canvas with linear filtering, to bound GPU time per frame. Tone mapping and sRGB output are done once in the final blit.

GSAP tweens uniforms on the paused registered timeline: uEmerge (fog density and fractal power morph), camera position/target along an authored path, and uLandscape (blends the SDF via smooth-min toward a domain-repeated terrain fold). Each update renders synchronously from the uniforms; there is no frame accumulation, so out-of-order seeks match.

Preview (3 s): reflective fractal solids emerge from dark fog with a slow dolly.
Full video: continues into the landscape and later the sunset. Sculptural lettering is planned as an SDF built from a precomputed glyph distance texture, extruded via max(d2D, |z|-h). It is not in the preview, and that limitation is reported.

tech.library_selection:

visual_cues: Powdery chalk marks on black paper with broken textured edges and layered opaque/pale strokes. Preserve a dark paper field; this differs from charcoal drawn on light paper.

tech.implementation:
Canvas 2D on an opaque #15141A field. A static black-paper tooth texture is generated once into an offscreen canvas from seeded noise2D (low-contrast speckle) and drawn first each frame.

Each chalk stroke is an authored path whose points are sampled at fixed arc-length steps once, cached with tangents. Rendering a stroke up to progress p stamps small irregular dabs of #F1EBDD along the cached samples:
- dab alpha is modulated by noise2D(x, y), which is spatial and seeded, so the same pixel always gets the same grain;
- 'paper tooth' gaps come from destination-out using the cached tooth texture threshold;
- edges break up via a noise-perturbed dab radius.

Layering: pale passes draw at about 0.35 alpha and opaque accent passes at about 0.9, with chalk pressure varied per stroke parameter.

Every frame is rebuilt from scratch: clear, paper, then each stroke up to its timeline progress. Nothing accumulates, so backward and direct seeks are exact.

GSAP tweens per-stroke progress values in order on the paused registered timeline. Arrows drawn in chalk render the head only after the shaft samples reach the endpoint. Text inside chalk-drawn boxes reveals after the box stroke completes.

Preview (3 s): a simple subject is sketched in pale strokes, then opaque highlights are added.
Full video: reuses the stroke library.

visual_cues: Backlit warm light table with dark granular sand silhouettes, scraped negative-space lines and changing sand density. Light shines through gaps rather than illuminating a white page.
note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Fullscreen ShaderMaterial on a Three.js orthographic quad.

Canvas 2D rasterizes authored sand shapes (silhouettes) and scrape strokes into two cached mask textures, A and B, for each keyed drawing state.

The fragment shader computes sand density:
- mix(maskA, maskB, uMorph) blurred via a few mip samples, to get soft accumulation;
- minus scraped negative-space lines (an SDF of polylines passed as a texture, multiplied by uScrape progress);
- multiplied by high-frequency seeded hash grain (per-pixel grain fixed in screen space, so it does not swim).

Backlight transmission: color = mix(sandColor #3A291B, lightColor #F5E3B5, exp(-k * density)). Light therefore shines through thin sand and gaps rather than illuminating a white page, with a slight warm vignette of the table (still the #F5E3B5 family).

GSAP tweens uMorph, uScrape and the sand pour radius on the paused registered timeline, and every update re-renders from the uniforms.

Preview (3 s): a sand silhouette thins, a finger-scrape line cuts through, then the shape transitions to the next form.
Full video: chains more mask pairs. This is illustrative granular appearance, not a granular physics simulation.

Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

tech.library_selection:
A transmitted-light density field with fine grain suits a fragment shader. Canvas 2D masks give authored control over shapes.

visual_cues: Folded paper structures rise from hinged pages with visible tabs, paper thickness, contact shadows and consistent creases. Page mechanics drive the reveal.
note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
A perspective Three.js scene with a separately colored environment. The book is two page boards: thin BoxGeometry with visible paper thickness, carrying a #F1E5CE paper CanvasTexture with seeded subtle grain and #342B25 printed linework drawn in Canvas 2D.

Pop-up pieces are thin boxes parented to hinge pivots placed on crease lines, with visible tabs glued to the pages. Each piece angle is derived analytically from the single page-opening angle θ:
- V-fold: piece angles solve the closed-loop hinge constraint, precomputed as a function table of θ;
- parallel fold: the panel stays parallel to the spine.

Creases therefore stay consistent and page mechanics drive the reveal.

The procedural curl technique adds slight bend to large flaps from immutable rest vertices × bend(θ), followed by computeVertexNormals.

Lighting: soft key plus fill, PCFSoftShadowMap contact shadows on the pages, and an explicit ACES tone map with output sRGB checked against the paper tokens.

GSAP owns θ and the camera dolly on the paused registered timeline. onUpdate evaluates all transforms from θ and renders, so seeks are exact. Labels printed on pop-up panels live in the panel textures, so they appear with their container.

Preview (3 s): the book opens from 20° to 180° as one V-fold structure rises with shadows.
Full video: adds pages, each with its own θ track.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

tech.library_selection:
Depth, paper thickness and hinge mechanics are defining, so true 3D is required. Flat SVG cutouts would fake it.

Alternatives considered:
- XPBD was rejected: rigid-panel kinematics are exact, cheaper and deterministic.
- Blender is unavailable.
- Outline/crease edge passes would push toward a cel look.
- MeshToon would flatten the paper.

Tradeoff: hinge constraints must be authored per structure, and shadow-map resolution must be tuned to avoid acne on thin boards.

visual_cues: Overlapping translucent fibers, torn edges and colored tissue layers create underwater depth. Preserve light transmission and overlap rather than opaque cardstock shapes.
note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Canvas 2D on an opaque #172D3A underwater field.

Each tissue piece is an authored polygon (fish, kelp, light shafts) whose torn edge is generated once: the outline is subdivided and perturbed by seeded noise2D, then cached as Path2D. A fiber texture per piece is generated once offscreen: seeded noise speckle plus short random-but-seeded fiber strokes, with stored seeds.

Per frame, pieces are composited back-to-front with globalAlpha around 0.45–0.6 and source-over, so overlaps visibly compound color and light transmission reads through the stack. The fiber texture is overlaid via 'multiply' clipped to the piece, and a slightly lighter, thinner torn rim stroke shows the paper edge. Tissue hue tokens are additional approved colors only if supplied; otherwise they are derived as foreground #F2EEE1 tints, checked with chroma_js. No arbitrary hues are invented.

GSAP tweens per-piece transforms on the paused registered timeline: gentle sway, a drift parallax with depth-scaled offsets, and layer laydown. Every frame is redrawn from scratch.

Preview (3 s): layers settle into an underwater scene with slow overlapping drift.
Full video: extends the layer manifest.

Reviewed technology choice: Canvas 2D on an opaque #172D3A underwater field.

Each tissue piece is an authored polygon (fish, kelp, light shafts) whose torn edge is generated once: the outline is subdivided and perturbed by seeded noise2D, then cached as Path2D. A fiber texture per piece is generated once offscreen: seeded noise speckle plus short random-but-seeded fiber strokes, with stored seeds.

Per frame, pieces are composited back-to-front with globalAlpha around 0.45–0.6 and source-over, so overlaps visibly compound color and light transmission reads through the stack. The fiber texture is overlaid via 'multiply' clipped to the piece, and a slightly lighter, thinner torn rim stroke shows the paper edge. Tissue hue tokens are additional approved colors only if supplied; otherwise they are derived as foreground #F2EEE1 tints, checked with chroma_js. No arbitrary hues are invented.

GSAP tweens per-piece transforms on the paused registered timeline: gentle sway, a drift parallax with depth-scaled offsets, and layer laydown. Every frame is redrawn from scratch.

Preview (3 s): layers settle into an underwater scene with slow overlapping drift.
Full video: extends the layer manifest. Translucent overlap and fiber are 2D compositing problems that Canvas solves natively and deterministically.

Alternatives considered:
- PixiJS would offer GPU blend modes but adds a ticker and a dependency for modest layer counts.
- SVG mix-blend-mode with feTurbulence is slow and inconsistent at export.
- Three.js transparency adds sorting complexity without needed depth.

Tradeoff: palette is limited to supplied tokens unless approved tissue colors are provided, and that gap is reported.

visual_cues: Jewel-colored glass panes separated by dark leading project the same image onto a stone interior. Cool dim architectural space changes into colored transmitted light with physically coherent occlusion.
note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Three.js stone interior: box room with MeshStandardMaterial, cool dim gray stone, high roughness and procedural Canvas grain on a #101216 dark field.

Canvas 2D paints the stained-glass image once: jewel-colored panes separated by dark leading lines. The same CanvasTexture is used twice:
- as the emissive map of the window plane, and
- as SpotLight.map behind the window, projecting that image onto the floor and walls with castShadow.

The window frame and mullions occlude the light coherently via the shadow map. This is a projected-texture approximation, not physically accurate refraction or caustics, and is stated as such.

Post: EffectComposer with RenderPass, then UnrealBloomPass (strength 0 until the finale), then OutputPass for tone mapping and sRGB.

GSAP timeline on the paused registered clock:
1. Dim stone.
2. Blackout: light intensity to 0.
3. Light up: spotlight intensity and angle sweep, and the projected pattern moves across the floor.
4. Final white bloom: bloom strength and light intensity ramp up.

All values are pure functions of time.

Preview (3 s): dim → blackout → colored projection.
Full video: adds the white bloom finale and camera moves.

tech.implementation: Stage #101820. A procedural lens mechanism in a deterministic hierarchy: housing (steel #8196A5 PBR metal), lens elements (MeshPhysicalMaterial tinted #61D4DC, transmission approximated), retaining rings and an aperture. A cutaway uses a clipping plane with localClippingEnabled plus stencil caps or explicit cut-face geometry so there are no hollow faces. An internal light path is a TubeGeometry with #628BF4 → focus #EF9F5C as discrete segments. GSAP owns part offsets along the optical axis and a calm camera arc. SVG overlay labels are reprojected each seek with Vector3.project from part anchors. Leader lines draw with DrawSVGPlugin, and anchor dots or arrowheads (data-arrowhead-for) appear only when the stroke arrives. Label text uses data-reveal-after its caption backing (#EFF4F7 on a dark local card). 3s preview: assembled 0–0.5s → axial separation and cutaway 0.5–1.5s → held labeled path 1.5–2.4s → precise reassembly by 3s. glTF parts only if authorized assets are supplied.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. tech.implementation:
Raw WebGL2 fullscreen triangle at a bounded internal resolution (e.g. 640×360, upscaled), fragment-shader raymarch at ≤64 primary steps and ≤6 light steps through a 3D density/emission field. The field is seeded fBm noise advected analytically upward by uTime (buoyancy and curl offsets as closed-form functions of time, no feedback buffers). The temperature field maps through an explicitly approximate ramp: flame_core #FFF0BC → flame_amber #FFAD42 → flame_orange #F05A28, then cooling into smoke #747B86 that absorbs and scatters light (Beer–Lambert). An analytic stationary hearth/ground with coal #4B403A receives flicker light spill. Background #101218, exposure clamped. GSAP's paused timeline sets uTime, uIgnite and uCool; every seek redraws one frame. 3s preview: ignition 0–0.6s → tall readable flame 0.6–2.0s → cooling translucent smoke 2.0–3.0s. The caption states it is an illustrative procedural volume, not a combustion solver. Full physically simulated shots need Blender/Cycles gas simulation with baked frames; it is unavailable here and reported as missing. The explosion recipe uses staged deterministic shock radius and debris uniforms.
Optional recipe blast_aftermath: Stage ignition/compression, expanding force, displaced material and cooling aftermath. Keep causal propagation visible across several states; never replace it with one white flash. Use deterministic or baked volume/debris trajectories and coherent environmental response.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

tech.implementation: Preview: a single stable parchment page (#EFE4C8, seeded SVG grain, slightly darker deckle edge) with no camera tilt. Page grid: a vine border (red #A5433C, blue #3C5487, green #66825D, outlines #352D27), a decorated vector-interlace initial in its frame box, a framed original miniature, and an HTML/CSS text column in an approved font. Only verified copy goes in; otherwise the column shows blank ruling, never pseudo-script. Sequence: 0–0.9s, the initial's outline is drawn and then filled. 0.6–1.6s, the border draws, with leaf fills following each stroke. 1.2–2.2s, the miniature frame completes and only then does its interior art reveal (data-reveal-after = the frame id). 2.2–2.8s, a narrow masked highlight sweep over #B89B51 gilded shapes only, plus one small gesture. Hold. Full video options: (a) a page turn using Three.js procedural paper curl on a subdivided BufferGeometry page, with mirrored front/back CanvasTextures derived from the same SVG page so registration holds. Use XPBD only if physically constrained bending is required, and bake it. Alternatively an offline Blender/EEVEE bake, runtime unverified. (b) A slow push into the miniature using layered high-resolution assets. (c) Approved parchment scans prepared with Cropper/Pillow/Sharp under the vectors. Verified calligraphy assets replace the blank column when supplied.
