tech.implementation: Preview: a river landscape on #F0E9D7 built from about 6–10k seeded short brush dabs, with per-dab width, length and angle set by a seeded PRNG and authored flow fields per region. Colors come only from the sky #9EBCC8, foliage #829C79, sunlight #D8BF7A and rose #C59D9D families plus #364747 accents. Adjacent complementary touches give optical mixing, and distant layers have softer contrast. Static layers are rasterized once into offscreen canvases. Only the water reflection (about 1.5k dabs) and one small subject are redrawn, each dab's state a pure function of time t (shimmer = sin(t·ω+phase_i) on length and sunlight mix, with bounded jitter). 0–1.0s, regional paint-on driven by a per-dab threshold against GSAP progress. 1.0–3.0s, reflection shimmer and a slight grass sway, then hold. Disclose as a procedural approximation. Full video: approved or newly painted layered painting assets (for example Krita layers, runtime unverified) can replace procedural regions, animated per layer with only local motion. Drawing-asset paint-on sequences are stepped by time. For very large dab counts, precompute dab tables offline (NumPy) or switch the renderer to PixiJS sprites while keeping the same time-derived state.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

tech.library_selection: Thousands of broken marks are a Canvas workload. SVG DOM would be too heavy, and WebGL instancing adds complexity without better fidelity at this scale. p5.js and PixiJS are viable alternatives but add a lifecycle for no default gain. Animating only the reflection avoids the forbidden whole-image boil, and no blur or swirl filters are used, keeping it distinct from Post-Impressionism.

Approved layered illustration, high-resolution or PNG/SVG parallax layers keep the shallow offsets. Paper.js may author cloud-curl geometry. Fine bounded contours with translucent washes are vector-native, and DrawSVG enforces the contour-before-pigment rule. Canvas 2D adds only the silk texture. WebGL ink diffusion and Rough.js were rejected because they introduce uncontrolled splashes or sketchy lines. Parallax stays shallow so the painted plane is respected, and asset routes are listed as full-video options rather than preview defaults.

tech.implementation: Preview: a Three.js WebGLRenderer with a fixed orthographic full-frame quad and ShaderMaterial. GLSL computes a seeded fBm rock height field (base #AF845A with ochre #C49B6B and chalk #DDD0B4 variation) with pore cavities and finite-difference normals. Lighting is an explicit approximation: one broad warm light at a uniform position. Pigment comes from original animal contours (bison, horse) and a few hand stencils drawn once into a Canvas 2D texture as irregular-edged charcoal #3B2B21 and red #984B32 strokes, with seeded edge noise baked. The shader offsets pigment UVs by the height gradient so marks follow the relief, absorbs pigment more in cavities, and multiplies it over albedo. uReveal against a per-stroke order map reveals pigment in short meaningful strokes over 0–1.8s. Over 1.8–3.0s, uLightPos sweeps across while the rock stays fixed. GSAP tweens the uniforms proxy, and each update renders synchronously. No glow, cartoon lines or pseudo-inscriptions. Show a disclosure on screen or in credits: procedural rock and pigment approximation, not archaeological footage. Full video: cache the static height field and albedo in a WebGLRenderTarget, or use a displaced BufferGeometry relief with MeshStandardMaterial plus a normal map as an alternative. Precompute height and stroke-order maps offline (NumPy/Pillow). Authored pigment-application frame sequences or transparent hand-drawn marks can replace Canvas strokes. An approved rock photo may serve as albedo, still disclosed as composited. An offline Blender/Cycles or EEVEE relief bake (runtime unverified) is an optional higher-fidelity route.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Surface relief and a moving light are part of this medium, so a flat SVG would fake the material. A 2.5D shader height field is faithful, bounded and seekable, with lighting stated as approximate. Canvas 2D gives simple authored pigment strokes that GLSL wraps onto the relief. A Canvas-only route would be cheaper but could not move light across relief convincingly. Blender bakes and PBR realism are optional full-video routes, not defaults. Bloom was rejected because glow is forbidden.

Strokes are cached per segment, with seeded edge noise baked once. The shader samples the pigment UVs offset by the height gradient (strokes conform subtly to the relief), absorbs pigment less on raised grain and more in cavities, and multiplies over the rock albedo. Reveal: a uniform uReveal (0..1) compared against a per-stroke order map in a texture channel shows pigment in short meaningful strokes over 0–1.8s. 1.8–3.0s, a slow light passage sweeps uLightPos across the wall while the rock texture stays fixed. GSAP tweens a uniforms proxy, and each update renders synchronously from it, so seeks match sequential playback. No glow, cartoon lines or pseudo-inscriptions.
